[BUG] maybeRefreshPRBody replaces a coder-authored PR body with the reviewer summary after a fix cycle ## Bug Description `maybeRefreshPRBody` (`pkg/foreman/agent/executor_native.go`, called at line 1218 after a fix cycle) rebuilds the PR body from the **reviewer's summary** and calls `PullRequestUpdate` with it. Once #1768 lands (PR #1776), the PR body opened on review GO is the **coder's** `extra.modelExtra.prBody`, rendered through `githubpr.DescriptionBody`. The refresh path knows nothing about that: after the first fix cycle it overwrites the coder-authored description with a one-line grounded summary, and it does so without the template, the provenance line or the issue link that the open path renders. So the body a maintainer reads depends on whether the Workload iterated: zero iterations, coder description; one or more, reviewer sentence. #1768 fixed the open path only and named this as a separate issue, as does the commit on #1776. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Let the coder return GO with a populated `prBody`, the reviewer return NO-GO once, the coder fix, and the reviewer return GO. 3. Read the PR body and compare with `kubectl get agentictask <wl>-code-<N> -o jsonpath='{.status.result.extra.modelExtra.prBody}'`. ## Expected Behavior The refresh keeps the coder's description as the body and updates only what the fi

feat(downloader): log newline-terminated download progress ## What The `model-downloader` init container now logs download progress as newline-terminated lines, so `kubectl logs -c model-downloader` shows how a multi-gigabyte model download is going. ## Why Fixes #1895. curl's progress meter redraws in place with carriage returns, and Kubernetes records a log line only at a newline. After the first redirect the downloader log was silent until the transfer finished, so a healthy slow download was indistinguishable from a stalled one without `kubectl exec`. ## How Every curl transfer now runs under a shared `download_with_progress` shell helper (a `downloadProgressFn` const in `internal/controller/model_storage.go`). It backgrounds the transfer with `--no-progress-meter`, polls the partial's size every second, and prints ``` Downloaded 256 MiB of 18042 MiB (1%) ``` every `${PROGRESS_INTERVAL:-10}` seconds (a positive integer of seconds, overridable through the init container environment; default 10). `wait` carries the transfer's own exit status, so a failed download still fails the init container. The total is the `Content-Length` the HTTP resume/revalidate paths already read in their HEAD probe; `resumePrologue` now also exposes it as `$remote_size` for the heartbeat, mirroring `remoteRevalidateScript`. S3 and multi-file downloads that have no probe print bytes only (`Downloaded N MiB`). Reach: single-file HTTP IfNotPresent and OnChange, single-file S3, and all four multi-fil

The metal-agent path does the same. ## Why Fixes #1894. Without `--alias`, llama.cpp reports the namespaced file path as the model ID, which Open WebUI and every other OpenAI-compatible client show verbatim. Filed as a known limitation of #1738 rather than discovered later: the gap was identified while reviewing that change, and the change is still worth landing because the report is diagnostic-only and self-healing. feat(router): charge budgeted streams by requesting upstream usage ## What Charges budgeted streaming responses that carry no `usage` chunk. When a budget applies to a streamed request, the proxy rewrites the buffered request to set `stream_options.include_usage`, so the upstream reports the count it already has. ## Why The proxy charges from the provider's own count (#434/#1853). A streaming response that omits the usage object was charged zero, so a client could evade a cap by asking for `"stream": true`. Closes that gap. Fixes #1852 ## How - `internal/router/usage.go`: new `InjectStreamUsage` sets `stream_options.include_usage` only when the body is a stream and does not already carry `stream_options`. It preserves the other fields as raw JSON. - `internal/router/proxy.go`: calls it after budget admission, gated on `isStream && len(scopeKeys) > 0`, so unbudgeted traffic dispatches untouched. - `internal/router/proxy_test.go`: the fake backend gains an opt-in `honorUsage` SSE mode (off by default, so it still models a server that ignores the option) and captures the upstream body. New tests cover the injection reaching the upstream, unbudgeted traffic not being touched, and a compliant upstream charging a non-zero amount with the `no_usage` counter untouched. - `internal/router/usage_test.go`: table-driven `InjectStreamUsage` cases including existing `stream_options`, `stream: false`, empty, and non-JSON bodies. `RouterBudgetUnchargedTotal{reason="no_usage"}` still marks an

feat: hierarchical token and dollar budgets with audit log Part of epic #437. **Phase 2: Production hardening**. ## Scope **Budgets:** - Implement `BudgetSpec` (token caps, dollar caps, rolling window, scope key). - Scopes: per-router, per-rule, per-team (where team is derived from a configurable header like `x-llmkube-team`). - In-memory rolling counters for v0.1 (persistence in #11). Document the state-loss-on-restart limitation. - On budget exhaustion: return HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` and a structured error body indicating the exhausted budget. - Surface utilization in `.status.budgetUtilization` and as the `llmkube_router_budget_utilization` gauge (added in #9). **Audit log:** - Structured JSON to stdout for every routing decision: timestamp, request id, router, rule matched, backend selected, backend tier, classification, prompt token count, completion token count, estimated USD cost (computed from `RouterBackend.CostPerMillionTokens`), outcome (success/fail-closed/budget-exceeded/timeout/5xx). - Configurable via `policy.auditLog.sink`: `stdout` (default), `file` (path), `otlp` (forward to OTel collector as logs). MVP ships `stdout`; the others can be stubs that return `NotImplemented` until follow-up issues fill them in. ## Success criteria - Unit tests cover budget arithmetic (rolling window math, multi-scope precedence, overflow). - Integration test exceeds a budget within the window and verifies 429 + Retry-After. - Audit log entries are valid JSON and pass schema

fix(federation): enforce and honor the edge's heartbeat push cadence ## What Three commits against the FederatedCluster heartbeat interval: 1. Reject a sub-cadence value at admission and in the CLI (`fix(federation)`). 2. Make the hub derive staleness and its requeue from the cadence the edge delivers (`fix(federation)`). 3. Run `federation-chart-crds` in the gate, now that CI regenerates it (`fix(foreman)`). ## Why Fixes #1788. The CRD accepted `heartbeatIntervalSeconds` values the edge cannot deliver. The edge pushes on a fixed 30s cadence (`defaultFederationEdgeInterval`), and the hub derives its staleness thresholds from the spec value (3x Stale, 10x Unreachable), so an accepted 5..9 flips a healthy site to Stale between pushes. Option 1 from the issue: raise the floor to 30 so admission enforces the cadence the edge actually has, and reject the same values in `llmkube fleet register` with a message naming the floor rather than bouncing off the API server. Commit 2 is the half the issue's option 1 does not cover: the floor stops *new* sub-cadence values, but a site already registered below it keeps false-Staleing. The hub now clamps the spec interval up to the delivered cadence at both use sites (the phase derivation and the requeue), through one helper tied to `defaultFederationEdgeInterval`, so the two 30s cannot drift. ## How - `api/federation/v1alpha1/federatedcluster_types.go`: `Minimum=5` -> `Minimum=30`, with the CRD regenerated (`make manifests`, `make federation-

[FEATURE] Evaluate OCI ImageVolume (k8s 1.36 GA) as a model source ## Feature Description Kubernetes `ImageVolume` (the OCI VolumeSource) reached **GA and was locked in k8s 1.36**. It mounts an OCI artifact directly into a pod as a volume — meaning model weights can be pulled straight from a registry with **no init container and no download/puller step**. ## Problem Statement > As a fleet operator, I want model weights delivered by the same registry, credentials, and mirroring I already use for images, so that air-gapped and multi-node deployments do not need a separate download-and-cache path. LLMKube today stages weights via a download Job plus a model-cache PVC (`pvc://` sources, `spec.modelCache`). That path works, but it carries its own credential handling, cache-key logic, PVC lifecycle, and the oscillation class of bugs we have already hit (#928, #1139, #1353). ## Proposed Solution Evaluate, and if it holds up, add an OCI-artifact model source (e.g. `oci://`) backed by `ImageVolume`: - Weights become a normal OCI artifact — registry auth, mirroring, signing, and air-gapped import all reuse the container-image path we already document. - Removes the init-container/puller and the per-service cache PVC for that source type. - Complements rather than replaces `pvc://` and `s3://`; existing sources stay. Open questions to answer in the evaluation: k8s 1.36 floor (do we gate the source type on server version?), runtime support in the CRI versions we target, artifact layout f

feat(foreman): verify-equipped scan-gate loop reproducing image scans before the verdict ## What A verify-equipped **scan gate** for Foreman: an `AgenticTask` (or any `Workload` step) can declare `spec.scanGate`, and after every coder push the agent reproduces the release-image CVE gate (`hack/scan-images.sh`) in a clean-room Kubernetes Job — building the release images the way GoReleaser does and Trivy-scanning them — feeding findings back to the coder for fix rounds, bounded by `Agent.spec.maxScanIterations`. The deterministic verify stage also re-runs the scan before a `GATE-PASS` can stand on a scan-declared branch. ## Why Fixes #1798 CI's container-image scan was the one gate a coder agent couldn't see into: a branch could burn its whole envtest-clean push cycle and still die at the release scan on findings (`base_image`, `other`, `content`) that the agent never had a chance to address. fix(controller): keep generated args when a non-CLI runtime overrides command ## What `spec.command` no longer drops the runtime's generated args for runtimes that build no command of their own. The verbatim-args path from #1829 is now gated on the backend implementing `CommandBuilder` instead of on `spec.command` being set, and the `Command` field doc (and generated CRDs) spell out both behaviors for every runtime. ## Why Refs #1842 #1829 made any `spec.command` override mean "honor `spec.args` verbatim, drop the generated args". That is correct for the three backends that implement `CommandBuilder` (`vllm`, `sglang`, `personaplex`): handing `vllm serve <model> --host …` to a bring-your-own launcher breaks it. `llamacpp` implements no `CommandBuilder` — it serves via the image ENTRYPOINT plus generated args — so for it `spec.command` was only ever an entrypoint override. The result was a llamacpp InferenceService starting `llama-server` with no `--model`, and no `--ctx-size`, `--mmproj`, speculative-decoding flags or `--host`/`--port` either. fix(foreman): let the coder resolve a rebase conflict instead of failing loud Closes #1839. ## Problem On a pr-fix or revision, `setupTaskBranch` restores the prior attempt and `RebaseOntoBase` rebases it onto the current base. On **any** conflict it ran `git rebase --abort` and failed the task `INCOMPLETE` **before the coder loop ran** — so a PR that only needed its conflict resolved was abandoned to needs-human. A batch of PRs touching the same files makes this systematic: once one merges, every sibling conflicts on rebase and fails identically. The fail-loud was deliberate (#1042/#1364 — the old reset+overwrite behavior silently reverted merged work). But it left no path to actually *resolve* a legitimate conflict. ## Change Add a resolve path: - **`RebaseOntoBase`** gains `LeaveConflicts`. When set, a conflict leaves the workspace mid-rebase and returns a typed `*RebaseConflictError` naming the unmerged files instead of aborting. Default (`false`) keeps the exact pre-#1839 abort-and-fail contract for callers that cannot resolve. - **`setupTaskBranch`** uses `LeaveConflicts` on the rebase path; **`Execute`** treats `*RebaseConflictError` as a soft signal and hands the mid-rebase workspace to the coder loop, whose prompt leads with an instruction to resolve the conflict (keeping both the base's merged work and the branch's intent) and finish the rebase. - **Post-loop guard**: a coder GO is downgraded to `INCOMPLETE` (`RebaseConflictUnresolved`) if the workspace is still mid

fix(router): rewrite model to served name on IfIdle fall-through ## What The dispatcher rewrote the outbound `model` field only for backends with an explicit `Model`, which only external providers have, so a request that reached a local backend under a different client alias (an `IfIdle` rule skipping a busy non-resident ModelPool member and falling through to the warm one) still carried the alias; llama.cpp ignores the field but vLLM, SGLang and TGI answer `404 The model X does not exist`, which the proxy logged as a successful dispatch. Local backends now carry the name of the InferenceService they resolve to (the name their runtime serves) through the compiled wire config, and the dispatcher sends that when the backend declares no `Model`. A body whose `model` already matches is passed through unmodified instead of re-marshalled, so the common request stays byte-identical, and external backends keep using their declared `Model` exactly as before. ## Why Fixes #1835 ## How New `Backend.inferenceService` field on the proxy wire config, populated by the controller from `spec.backends[].inferenceServiceRef.name`, plus a `Backend.outboundModel()` helper the dispatcher uses in place of `backend.Model`. `applyModelOverride` gained an equality short-circuit. Covered by a unit test on `outboundModel`, a `Dispatch`-level test asserting the upstream receives the served name, a controller assertion that the field is compiled, and an extension to the existing `IfIdle` end-to-end proxy

When the last waiter for a member gave up, the deferred cleanup fired an asynchronous `Deactivate` outside the lock; a request for the same member arriving in that window started a swap and scaled the member up, and the stale `Deactivate` then scaled it back to zero. `Activate` is idempotent-by-check and never re-issued, so the swap goroutine waited on a member that could never become Ready. That goroutine had no deadline either: its only exit was the cancel fired when the last waiter for the target left, so a client retrying on 503 kept the doomed swap alive indefinitely. `swapping` stayed true, the resident member's fast path stayed closed, and every request on the pool burned its hold budget and 503ed, including requests for the member that was still loaded. ## How The deferred deactivate stays asynchronous but now re-takes the lock and re-checks before patching, skipping itself when the member is wanted again: a waiter has arrived, it became resident, or a swap newer than the generation the deactivate was scheduled against is activating it. But `generic` has no request-aware idle probe — `GenericBackend`'s `/health` always reads idle, so in a swap-based ModelPool a busy backend is reclaimed mid-request. A custom entrypoint owns its args, and the documented `extraArgs` escape hatch still applies under any runtime. Runtimes whose `BuildArgs` already returns `spec.Args` (`generic`) are unaffected — the existing moshi (generic) `spec.command` test still passes.
